glance.what: A robotic arm filming cinematic product showcases for ads.
glance.why: unclear

record.what_it_is: A phone web app where a user speaks or types a request and an SO-101 robot arm with a wrist camera films a product with one of three cinematic moves, then returns the clip to the app at the requested length. Perceptron Mk1.5 parses the request and picks the angle.
record.problem_and_user: Small sellers and creators who want dynamic product-ad footage without manual camera work.
record.one_line_pitch: Voice- or text-commanded SO-101 robot arm with a camera that films products from dynamic cinematic angles using a trained movement policy.
record.problem_statement: Dynamic-angle product videos are laborious to shoot; the team wanted algorithmic robot cinematography that is smooth and efficient.
record.devpost_tagline: We created a system for cinematic product showcases and ads with perceptron's SO-101 robotic arm.
devpost_first_sections: Many advertisements of smaller products like smartphones, wearable devices, foods, and more showcase in dynamic angles to better appeal to viewers. Seeing how the SO-101 robotic arm moves around with its attached camera reminded us of this, and gave us the idea to replicate that cinematography using algorithms, making the process more streamlined, smooth, and efficient.

There are two parts to the project, the app and the arm. The app has voice and text input for users to command the arm, and then after the arm moves around and records at various angles, it sends the video back to the user on the app. The arm then is the second part, and it rotates and traverses around any product using 1 of 3 different dynamic movements as it records.

glance.what: Automatic video editor that cuts pauses and mistakes while recording.
glance.why: Removes editing work by cutting pauses and errors automatically.

record.what_it_is: Browser recorder that edits itself while you talk. Audio streams to a backend that transcribes it, an OpenAI tool-calling agent decides which segments to cut, and ffmpeg trims and stitches the clip; it can also post to Instagram Reels.
record.problem_and_user: Short-form video creators who lose time re-recording or cutting pauses and flubbed takes after the fact.
record.one_line_pitch: Browser recorder that edits video live while you speak, trimming pauses and bad takes via speech-to-text plus an OpenAI tool-calling agent and ffmpeg, with optional Reels posting.
record.problem_statement: Recording clean video means re-takes and long manual editing to cut mistakes and pauses.
record.devpost_tagline: An opinionated, automatic video editor that cuts out pauses and errors on the fly. Just press record, ready or not, because you literally cannot make a mistake.
devpost_first_sections: Ever fumble through a video recording, pause awkwardly, or restart mid-sentence? Typical video editing means recording everything, then spending hours re-recording or cutting out mistakes - but what if your video could edit itself while you recorded?

ViniClip is an opinionated, automatic video editor that cuts out pauses and errors on the fly. Record yourself directly in your browser, and ViniClip removes awkward pauses, repeated takes, or any mistake you wish to get rid of instantly. The final product is a video that's ready to post immediately, you can even command the video to be upload to Instagram reels instantly.

glance.why: Helps kids with alexithymia recognize emotions through fun games.

record.problem_statement: Children with autism or alexithymia struggle to read facial expressions, and conventional education rarely supports this.
record.devpost_tagline: Echo assists neurodivergent kids that struggle with alexithymia in learning how to differentiate facials expressions and emotions fun with games, animations, and a mascot that mirrors you!

glance.why: unclear

record.problem_and_user: Young children, parents and teachers; static alphabet books lack interactivity and some learners struggle to visualize concepts.
record.one_line_pitch: Mobile AR app that recognizes a scanned book page and overlays a 3D model and AI-generated explanation video.
record.target_user: children and students using printed books
record.problem_statement: Static book pages make learning less engaging for children.
record.devpost_tagline: Transforming every page into a 3D learning journey. AlphaBuddy AR helps you visualize the contents in a page, enabling better learning experince, more immersive and imaginative.
devpost_first_sections: The inspiration for Alphabuddy AR came from the desire to make learning visual. Some people don't experience mental imagery making it harder for people to imagine and visualise, especially in subjects like Mathematics. Additionally, We also noticed that traditional alphabet books, while essential for early education, often lack the excitement and interactivity that can captivate young learners. We wanted to bridge the gap between traditional education and cutting-edge technology.

Alphabuddy AR is a groundbreaking software that leverages augmented reality (AR) to enhance the learning experince by creating a 3d model and an explanation video on top of the page you scan. When a book page featuring some content and pictures is scanned with our app, it comes to life! The app generates AI-driven videos that explain each letter, along with AR objects that add a fun and interactive dimension to the learning process. Children can explore, interact with, and gain a deeper understanding of each letter in a way that was never possible before.

glance.what: Pirate-themed treasure hunt game using photos of real locations.
glance.why: unclear

record.what_it_is: Pirate-themed photo scavenger game in Streamlit: players pick an image another user uploaded and try to find where it was taken, then upload their own photo from the spot; GPS from EXIF and CNN image similarity decide whether they found the treasure.
record.problem_and_user: Geocaching and GeoGuessr style fun for players who like location puzzles and uploading challenges.
record.one_line_pitch: Streamlit game where players try to find where a user-uploaded photo was taken and upload their own shot, which is scored against it by image comparison.
record.problem_statement: Geocaching-style photo hunts need an automatic way to verify that a player reached the right spot.
record.devpost_tagline: Land Ahoy! Set sail across the seven seas to seek out buried treasures, with clues hidden in images ye share! Aye, capture all seven treasures, and may the wind be at yer back!
devpost_first_sections: Our inspiration for this project was geocaching, geoguessing, and treasure hunts in general. We wanted the user to participate in challenges to find where another user took an image. The goal was to emulate how pirates would hunt for treasure given obscure clues. A player can choose to try and find the location of any image that is uploaded by any user.

The application was built using the Streamlit framework and MongoDB (deployed using AWS) for data persistence. A user can choose between many user-uploaded images, and try to find where exactly this image was taken. To validate the attempts of the user, their uploads are compared with the chosen image in two ways–GPS location proximity and image similarity (using a CNN that calculates the cosine similarity between two images). If the user successfully found the location of the image, they have found “the treasure”! This achievement is saved to their profile which holds information about what other “treasures” they have found.

glance.what: Detects objects and hands with distances, guiding users by sound.
glance.why: Helps visually impaired people navigate daily life through sound.

record.problem_and_user: Visually impaired people wanting affordable mobility and independence; cites 7.3 million visually impaired US adults.
record.one_line_pitch: iPhone camera and LiDAR app that guides visually impaired users around obstacles and to objects using spatial audio in AirPods.
record.problem_statement: Visually impaired people lack affordable, accessible tools for navigating everyday surroundings independently.
record.devpost_tagline: Helping the visually impaired navigate their daily life - through sound.
devpost_first_sections: VisionNav is built with a focus on aiding the visually impaired who are looking for an easily accessible way to navigate their daily lives. The reason behind creating such an app is most of our team knows someone in their family who may face difficulties with vision. With further research into this topic, we found that 7.3 million adults in the U.S. are classified as visually impaired, with 1 million fully blind, of which 70% are unemployed. This reality inspired us to create VisionNav as an affordable solution that not only simplifies everyday navigation but also fosters independence and empowers users with the confidence to thrive in their communities.

VisionNav utilizes the built-in phone camera and LIDAR in an iPhone to stream a real-time visualization of the user's surroundings, and uses sound within devices like the AirPods to navigate around the setting. Within this setting, VisionNav aims to accomplish three different categories of tasks. glance.what: Wearable band and plush cat that interrupts anxiety before it peaks.
glance.why: Catches anxious movement early, acting before panic peaks.

record.what_it_is: A hardware prototype for anxiety and panic support: a wrist band with an accelerometer streams motion, a Random Forest flags agitation, and the system responds with paced haptic breathing and a plush cat whose ears move and that speaks calming prompts.
record.problem_and_user: People having anxiety or panic attacks who cannot operate a phone app in the moment; later direction for children and families.
record.one_line_pitch: Wristband with accelerometer detects rising agitation and delivers paced haptic breathing, paired with a plush cat that moves its ears and speaks grounding prompts.
record.target_user: people with anxiety and panic attacks, including children
record.problem_statement: During panic attacks people cannot operate phones or apps, so help needs to arrive without any action from them.
record.devpost_tagline: A band and a plush cat that catch anxiety in how you move — and interrupt it before it peaks. There's no app to open, no waiting room. It's already on you, already watching, and it acts first.
devpost_first_sections: I(Wenqing) spent three years as a mental-health clinician, sitting with people in the grip of anxiety and panic attacks. Anxiety is the most common mental illness in the U.S.: about 40 million adults live with an anxiety disorder, and roughly 1 in 11 people has at least one panic attack a year. A panic attack is not "just stress." Your hands are shaking, you can't breathe, and you're certain you're about to die. It is one of the most frightening things a body can go through, and it contributes to nearly 11,000 suicide deaths in the U.S. every year. How do people cope today? Therapy genuinely works, but your clinician is not always in the room when the attack actually hits. Apps can help, but

TheraCat is a two-part companion: a wristband and a soft plush cat. The wristband quietly watches how you move. When it picks up the motion patterns associated with agitation and rising arousal, TheraCat acts first, before you have to do anything at all. TheraBot’s detection prototype is a minimal end-to-end pipeline for identifying simulated wrist-motion arousal from MPU6050-style accelerometer data. It generates synthetic three-axis acceleration signals for two states: Calm and Agitated. Calm motion is smoother and lower-variance, while agitated motion has higher variability, larger oscillations, sharper spikes, and more irregular wrist movement. glance.why: Organizes technician work orders and routes in one platform.

record.problem_and_user: Data center technicians and ops admins using fragmented tools where errors are costly.
record.one_line_pitch: Operations command center for data-center technicians covering AI ticket parsing from email and Slack, health-aware routing on floor plans, predictive inventory and a device assistant.
record.problem_statement: Data-center technicians use fragmented tools and manual processes, causing human error and inefficiency in large compute facilities.
record.devpost_tagline: A platform that supports data center technicians in a multitude of daily tasks, from planning out optimal routes to complete work orders, generating tickets from emails of incidents, and more!
devpost_first_sections: DC Daddy - NMC DataCenter Command Center

Data centers are the backbone of modern computing, yet technicians managing $2.8 billion facilities powering 400MW of compute still rely on fragmented tools and manual processes. We were inspired by NMC's challenge of reducing human error and operational inefficiency in environments where a single mistake can cost millions. We saw an opportunity to build an integrated command center that transforms how data center operations work, making technicians' jobs smarter, not harder, while prioritizing their health and safety.

glance.what: AR Spectacles lens guiding people through disasters and emergencies.
glance.why: Guides people hands-free through natural disasters via AR glasses.

record.what_it_is: A Snap Spectacles AR lens built in Lens Studio that guides a user through an earthquake: it scans the room, labels objects, gives audio and visual cues for safe spots, and shows a voice-controlled floating checklist.
record.problem_and_user: People in natural disasters, with earthquakes as proof of concept; many wrongly think running to doorways is safest.

glance.why: Turns doomscrolling into studying by tracking completed courses.

record.what_it_is: A SvelteKit study app that turns course uploads into short 'reels' and makes scrolling the way through learning: theory reels teach, test reels quiz, and correct answers advance a progress bar.
record.problem_and_user: Students like doomscrolling but find studying rigid; the app channels the scroll habit into a structured learning flow.
record.one_line_pitch: A study tool that turns the doomscroll gesture into a structured learning flow, with each scroll advancing the student through material.
record.problem_statement: Students prefer effortless scrolling over rigid studying, so the app channels that habit into learning.
record.devpost_tagline: Doomscrolling was added to the Dictionary in 2025, a clear shift in how we consume information, instead of fighting it, we thought, what if we designed an app to help you study whilst Doom scrolling.
devpost_first_sections: 🌱 Bloomscroll: Studying While Doomscrolling

Bloomscroll started with a very honest realization: We all wanted to doomscroll but we also needed to study. Scrolling is effortless, familiar, and strangely comforting. Studying, on the other hand, often feels rigid and demanding. Instead of fighting that instinct, we asked a different question: What if scrolling itself could become the study method? Rather than resisting the doomscroll, Bloomscroll embraces it, adapting the habitual vertical scroll into a structured learning flow . Each scroll pushes the student forward cognitively, not just visually. Our goal wasn’t to eliminate distraction, but to redirect it to something positive.

We were inspired by the Statefarm Challenge and NVIDIA Challenge to implement our skills in API version control and documentation to solve a high impact problem all developers face regularly when working with APIs.

When it doesn’t, it becomes a blind spot — regardless of severity. glance.why: Gets out-the-door car quotes without endless dealer calls.

record.problem_and_user: Car buyers waste days phoning dealers, repeating themselves and waiting on hold to compare prices and availability for one model.

record.problem_statement: Car shoppers waste days calling dealers, waiting on hold and repeating the same questions.

Finding your ideal car should be an enjoyable experience, free from endless calls, multiple dealership visits, repetitive conversations, browsing numerous websites, and waiting on hold. We know how frustrating it is to spend days comparing prices and checking availability for one model. That's why Toyoda was developed — a friendly, AI-driven calling assistant that handles all the hard work, making your car shopping smoother and more convenient enjoyable.

glance.what: Wearables and computer vision detect medical emergencies at large events.
glance.why: Alerts staff instantly so medical help arrives faster.

record.what_it_is: An event-safety prototype that pairs a Galaxy Watch (heart rate and vitals) with camera-based posture analysis on a server to detect fainting or dizziness in at-risk attendees, then alerts staff through a companion app with location and an AI-written incident summary.
record.problem_and_user: People with conditions such as POTS risk fainting in long, crowded event lines where response is slow; aimed at at-risk attendees and event medical staff.
record.one_line_pitch: Event safety system pairing a Wear OS watch with camera-based posture analysis to detect fainting or dizziness in at-risk attendees and alert medical staff.
record.target_user: event attendees with chronic conditions and event medical staff
record.problem_statement: People with conditions like POTS risk fainting in long event queues, and response to medical distress in crowds is slow.
record.devpost_tagline: Vigil pairs wearables with computer vision to detect medical emergencies at large events — alerting on-site staff instantly with a location and incident summary. Faster help, when it matters most.
devpost_first_sections: One of our team members has a relative with POTS — a condition that causes dizziness and fainting, especially after standing for long periods. Waiting in line at a concert shouldn't be a medical risk, but for people with chronic or episodic conditions, it often is. That personal experience drove us to build Vigil, and while POTS was our starting point, the real vision is broader: a scalable safety system that lets high-risk individuals participate in large events with confidence

Vigil is a safety system designed for people with conditions much like POTS attending large events. It combines a wearable medical assistance watch with computer vision monitoring to detect signs of potential medical distress. The wearable collects data related to the user's condition, while the computer vision system monitors posture and movement patterns that may indicate dizziness or fainting. If Vigil detects a potential medical emergency, it can alert medical personnel so help can arrive faster. Vigil helps reduce the risk of delayed response times and allows users to participate in crowded events with greater confidence.

record.problem_and_user: Campaign and ad teams wanting voters to see how a candidate's policies affect their locality; team cites interviews with 70+ campaigns and 40+ ad teams.
record.one_line_pitch: Multi-agent web app that generates personalised, state-compliant campaign ads where a politician's cloned voice and lip-synced video address a voter's local issues.
record.problem_statement: Voters feel disconnected from politicians and campaigns lack tools to show how policies affect individual voters.
record.devpost_tagline: Bringing politicians and voters closer, one personalized ad at a time.
devpost_first_sections: It feels like elections are taking up an increasing portion of our mindshare, with every election cycle it only gets more insane. Constantly flooded by news, by opinions – it's like we never get a break. And yet, paradoxically, voters feel increasingly less connected to their politicians. They hear soliloquies about the terrible deeds of the politician's opponent, but rarely about how their policies will affect them personally. That changes today. It's time we come back to a democracy which lives by the words E pluribus unum – from many, one. Citizens should understand exactly how politician's policies will affect them and their neighbours, and from that, a general consensus may form. And ca

Rally helps politicians meet voters where they are – in a figurative and digital sense. Politicians and campaign teams can use our platform to send geographically relevant campaign advertisements to voters – tailored towards issues they care deeply about. We thoroughly analyze the campaigner's policies to give a faithful representation of their ideas through AI-generated advertisements – using their likeness – and cross-correlate it with issues the voter is likely to care, and want to learn more, about. We avoid the uncanny valley with our content, we maintain compliance, and we produce content that drives voter engagement.

glance.what: Agent passively summarizes coding sessions to rebuild context later.
glance.why: Lets developers resume projects without losing their context.

record.what_it_is: A tool that tracks files changed during a coding session in VS Code, then sends the changelog and git status to an LLM to write a summary of what was done. Past sessions are searchable in a web dashboard, so a developer can recover context.
record.problem_and_user: Students and developers who juggle several projects and lose the reasoning behind their work.
record.one_line_pitch: Agentic dev tool that watches coding sessions in VS Code and generates searchable summaries so developers can regain context after switching projects.
record.target_user: student and hobbyist developers juggling several projects
record.problem_statement: Students switching between coding projects lose the reasoning, pending tasks and mental model behind their code.
record.devpost_tagline: Working Memory is an agentic workflow that passively observes your coding sessions, summarizes your progress, and reconstructs context from your history, enabling seamless re-entry into any project.
devpost_first_sections: As students who juggle between coding projects for classes, clubs, research, or personal work, we often face the problem of constantly switching between contexts. Every time we switch, we lose fragments of our working memory, which encompasses the reasoning behind decisions, pending tasks we may have, and the overall mental model of the code. For this reason, we created Working Memory , an agentic workflow that passively observes your work and automatically reconstructs context, enabling seamless re-entry into any project.

Working Memory connects your VS Code workspace to an AI-powered backend that continuously records and interprets your development sessions. Start a session : Initialize a coding session directly within the web dashboard. Code as usual : Any modified or newly created files are tracked. Stop the session : The changelog is gathered and fed into an AI data-processing pipeline, producing: A natural-language summary containing a high-level overview and actionable insights. Structured metadata containing the git status output. View History : The results appear in the web dashboard under Past Workflows, complete with a search engine for re-entering context later.

devpost_first_sections: Intern onboarding often feels overwhelming. New hires are handed hundreds of pages of PDFs, manuals, and policies, and are expected to absorb them quickly. We’ve gone through this ourselves and realized that traditional onboarding is both time-consuming for HR and ineffective for interns. We wanted to build a system that transforms static documentation into personalized, interactive lessons that make learning faster and more engaging.

Cognita takes company documents and turns them into interactive learning experiences. Companies upload training materials, and interns can then ask questions about their roles or processes. Instead of a generic answer, Cognita generates a short, tailored lesson with multiple sections. Each section can include interactive components such as multiple choice questions, fill-in-the-blanks, code examples, drag-and-drop activities, or diagrams. Progress is tracked automatically so both interns and companies can see how knowledge is being absorbed.

devpost_first_sections: As digital purchases becomes more mainstream making physical money less tangible, it's hard for kids to visualize their money and spending habits. In pursuit of teaching younger kids how to finance with their own money and games, Spendy is here to help!

Kids will have a Spendy card that can be spend on their favorite games. They will need to tap their card to authenticate their purchase for Robux or Valorant Points. Parents can overview their children purchase history and reload the Spendy card.

glance.what: Robotic arm rig meant to act like a cursor for surgery.
glance.why: Gives surgeons precise, fluid control like a cursor.

record.what_it_is: A four-arm robotic surgery demo station where a surgeon wearing a Quest 3 headset moves a physical camera arm by head tracking and issues natural-language commands that LLMs turn into arm motions. Includes a custom kinematics stack and Lean proofs that trajectories stay in safe bounds.
record.problem_and_user: Surgeons facing OR cost and specialist shortages; current surgical robots add precision but not automation because AI spatial vision and AI-to-robot control are weak.
record.one_line_pitch: Four-arm magnetically controlled robot surgery station steered by natural-language commands and a Quest 3 head-tracked camera, with Lean-verified trajectory safety.
record.problem_statement: Surgical specialist shortages and costly operating rooms; current surgical robots add precision but do not automate tasks or reduce staffing.
record.devpost_tagline: Cursor for surgery.
devpost_first_sections: The United States is facing a growing shortage of surgical specialists, projected to reach nearly 20,000 by 2036. Additionally, operating rooms cost roughly $2,200 per hour per surgeon. Today’s robotic surgical robots greatly improve precision by scaling and filtering human motion. But they do not automate surgical tasks. This is due to a lack of reliable AI spatial vision understanding and AI robot communication. Instead of making surgeries more accessible, current robots only make them more complex and costly.

Robosurge is a remotely controlled integrated surgery platform. It allows for a single surgeon to perform entire complex procedures autonomously from anywhere in the world. In traditional surgeries, an attending surgeon commands a large team of assistant surgeons. The attending surgeon syncs to Robosurge’s camera arm via a Meta Quest 3 VR. Then the surgeon can command an array of magnetically controlled robotic arms using natural language. This architecture reduces required personnel from 10 -> 1, and distance to patient from meters to anywhere around the world.

record.problem_and_user: Budget-conscious college students eating out who want filling, relatively healthy and affordable choices and cannot easily judge nutrition per dollar from a menu.

record.problem_statement: Eating out is hard when you must match meals to personal nutrition goals and restrictions.
record.devpost_tagline: Because every bite counts! Have you ever struggled to decide what to eat when you're going out? Don't worry, CuratePlate is here!
devpost_first_sections: As broke college students who love food, we often struggle to pick affordable, filling, and (relatively) healthy options when we're going out to eat. We wanted a solution to this problem, a way for us to see how "efficient" a meal is, how much we're getting from each dollar we spend.

Our app is personalized to each user. A user will input their height, weight, age, and biological sex, which we'll use to estimate their daily nutritional needs. The user can also update any dietary restrictions they may have. The user can use their camera to take a picture of a restaurant's menu. CuratePlate will then analyze all the options on the menu and create a customized score for it based off each individual user's information. The user can select any option on the menu they want to learn more about, and the app will show them all the necessary information. There is a Meal Value score, which is a value out of 100 that represents how economically efficient the option is for its price.

Using a physics based approach, we could correctly identify all ~4000 chords in an octave and rank them by dissonance. With the power of LLMs in today's world, it is easier than ever to offload the burden of improvisation to LLMs. However, it was important to us in the beginning of this process to stray away from the LLM models that have little interpretability. This way of constructing the chords and ranking their dissonance from the ground up builds concrete understanding of which chord works well with what. Now, introducing ChromaChord, a solution at the intersection of acoustics,

ChromaChord is a real-time AI jazz assistant that listens to your improvisation and helps you navigate harmony. As you play, it analyzes incoming notes using chroma vector representations, maps harmonic relationships onto a graph of possible chord transitions, and suggests musically coherent next chords. Of course, humans have limitations, and there are only so many paths we can physically traverse. So after the extensive sifting with the chroma vectors, we can use AI to generate harmony, melodies, matching the progression that was played.

glance.why: Finds customers early using business activity signals.

record.what_it_is: A lead-finding research agent for tradespeople. A contractor sets a trade and territory, and Klane searches public news, permits, procurement notices and announcements, filters them for relevance and currentness, plots prospects on a map with evidence dossiers, and models bid economics. The same agent is reachable by iMessage.
record.problem_and_user: Contractors such as roofers who spend evenings combing permit portals and announcements for future work before any contractor request is posted.
record.one_line_pitch: Lead-finding agent for tradespeople that researches public news, permits, procurement notices and announcements to surface upcoming work matched to a trade and territory.
record.target_user: small contractors and tradespeople such as roofers
record.problem_statement: Contractors spend evenings hunting permit portals and notices to find future jobs before they are posted.
record.devpost_tagline: Your next job is hiding in the headlines. Klane turns news, permits, and business activity into contractor leads - on a map or over text.
devpost_first_sections: Klane Your next customer is out there. Klane helps you find the evidence.

A roofing contractor should not have to spend their evening searching permit portals, procurement notices, and expansion announcements to find tomorrow’s work. Useful signals often appear before someone posts a straightforward request for a contractor. We wanted to connect those scattered clues to the right trade, location, and next step, in an interface people could use between jobs. The design combines Carolina blue with Frutiger Aero’s sense of space and movement: an interactive globe, frosted controls, and a transition into a local opportunity map.

glance.what: Monitors pipelines and predicts likelihood of hydrate buildup.
glance.why: Warns about hydrate risk before pipelines clog.

record.what_it_is: Dashboard for pipeline owners that predicts hydrate blockages in oil pipelines with a random-forest model trained on the sponsor's data. It offers trend charts, an alerts page, manual data entry for predictions and email notices.
record.problem_and_user: Pipeline owners who need early warning of hydrate formation, which can freeze gas flow during rapid pressure drops and endanger people and the environment.
record.one_line_pitch: Random-forest model trained on the sponsor dataset predicts hydrate blockages in oil pipelines, shown on a dashboard with live alerts and email notices.
record.problem_statement: Hydrate blockages in oil and gas pipelines are dangerous and harmful to the environment and hard to catch early.
record.devpost_tagline: Monitor your pipes and and the likelihood that there is a hydrate!
devpost_first_sections: We were inspired by our goal to build a full stack application with machine learning in conjecture with the datasets given by the EOG Resources challenge. We also realized the dangers of hydration caused by pipeline blockages in oil wells to humans and the natural environment, and have decided to make ourselves busy in attempt to solve this problem. As a group, we have not had much experience working on group programming projects together, and have found this challenge a great opportunity for us and for society as a whole.

Our project, PipeBrains, was trained using a machine learning algorithm from Scikit on the given datasets by EOG. It produced promising results, with an R^2 of around 94% and lesser mean error. With this, our trained model was able to predict possible hydrates in the pipes, as well as create the chart API to graph trends for the user to view. Moreover, we also added an alerts tab that shows alerts every second based on the data fed on pipes. We also added a custom field for owners to manually input data to for them to know the predictions. Firebase was used to manage login pages for the owners.

record.problem_and_user: Unbanked and underbanked people sharing rent, groceries and utilities, who currently rely on cash pooling or reimbursement apps that depend on timely repayment.
record.one_line_pitch: Group expense splitting app that charges each participant card at the moment of purchase instead of having one person front the money and be reimbursed later.
record.target_user: unbanked and underbanked groups, college-age roommates
record.problem_statement: Unbanked and underbanked people sharing rent and groceries rely on informal pooling or post-payment reimbursement, which is unreliable.
record.devpost_tagline: Lumo: Split expenses instantly, no upfront payments. Empowering seamless, real-time cost-sharing for everyone—fast, fair, and hassle-free. 💸⚡
devpost_first_sections: Unbanked and some underbanked individuals who lack access to traditional financial services face significant challenges in managing shared expenses such as rent, utilities, and groceries. These individuals are forced to rely on informal pooling like collecting physical cash or digital P2P payment tools like Zelle, PayPal, and Splitwise, which all facilitate post-transaction reimbursements. However, these methods are unreliable, as they depend on timely repayments, leaving the individual who fronts the payment vulnerable to delayed or unfulfilled reimbursements. For those already struggling with cash flow, this delay creates more financial strain. We believe that enabling real-time, equitable

Lumo enables people to split purchases in real-time at the point of purchase, unlike traditional P2P payment methods like Venmo, Zelle, PayPal, Apple Pay, and Splitwise, which require one person to pay upfront and rely on post-transaction reimbursements. Lumo directly divides payments among participants by charging the cards the users put on file. By integrating with existing payment methods like prepaid cards and ACH, Lumo provides an inclusive solution for unbanked and underbanked individuals, empowering them to manage shared expenses transparently and equitably.

record.what_it_is: A mobile app concept where a patient photographs a wound and a TensorFlow CNN returns a wound class with per-class confidence scores, with wound information kept in one place. Repo is a thin React scaffold with a LiveKit assistant folder.
record.problem_and_user: Patients managing one or more wounds who want easier tracking and information, also pitched to clinicians.
record.one_line_pitch: Mobile app concept that classifies wound photos with a CNN, shows confidence scores, and helps patients track healing.
record.problem_statement: Patients managing wounds lack an easy way to monitor healing and get a quick classification of wound type.
record.devpost_tagline: Voice to Text Rapid Response LLM to address immediate health issues.
devpost_first_sections: The wound tracking app is designed to be a comprehensive tool for patients who are undergoing wound care. Its primary goal is to support patients in their wound care journey and make it easier for them to monitor the healing process. The app aims to improve patient engagement and increase their sense of self-efficacy in wound care, by providing them with easy access to important information about their wounds. This can be incredibly beneficial for patients who are managing multiple wounds, as it provides them with a centralized place to store and review their wound information.

The application aims to develop a computer vision system that classifies and diagnoses wounds through image processing and convolutional neural network (CNN) techniques. The system will use digital images of wounds as input and perform image processing to extract features relevant to wound diagnosis. The features will be fed into the CNN model, which will classify the wound into different types and provide a diagnosis of the wound's severity. The model will be trained on a large dataset of wound images and annotations to achieve high accuracy in wound classification and diagnosis.

record.what_it_is: A silent speech-to-text prototype: lip geometry from video is matched to a personalized viseme reference set, converted to phonemes, and an LLM with Supermemory context turns them into a sentence, served as a Modal FastAPI endpoint.
record.problem_and_user: People in libraries, meetings or noisy places where speaking to voice typing is awkward, and people with speech difficulties.
record.one_line_pitch: Background lip-reading dictation: press a key, record the mouth, decode visemes to phonemes to words, and an LLM turns them into a sentence typed anywhere.
record.target_user: people in loud or quiet settings, speech-impaired users
record.problem_statement: Voice typing is awkward or impossible in noisy or quiet public places, and speech-impaired users lack fast input.
record.devpost_tagline: Voicepille was 2025. In 2026, you don’t need to use your voice. Press a key, & Vizem turns lip movements into text 5× faster than typing - its like speaking, but quieter, less awkward & more private.
devpost_first_sections: Our Story

We were trying to talk to someone from the Modal team during the hackathon, and it was kinda awkward since there were so many people and so much noise around us. We realised what it would be like working with so much noise and people. Voice typing is so much faster than regular typing, and we've been using it for a while, but we thought: how could you do it with that much clutter and around noise? So we built Vizem Flow - an agent that works in the background and, with a click on the keyboard, reads your lips and outputs text wherever you want it to.
